report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1 of daedalus/council/vendors.py: module docstring, constants, identity functions, VendorReply and FloorRefusal dataclasses. All claims checkable in this chunk are kept; claims about external behavior are uncheckable.
risks: vendor_reply_validation | medium | VendorReply.__post_init__ validates status/lane but no closed-set validation for reason or channel; a malformed reason could slip through. | Inspect rest of file for validation of reason against UNAVAILABLE_REASONS or rule labels.

handoff.purpose: Module docstring, closed vocabularies, identity helpers, VendorReply and FloorRefusal dataclasses.

symbols.name: STATUSES
symbols.note: Tuple of five transport statuses: ok, unavailable, timeout, refused_by_floor, error.

symbols.name: LANES
symbols.note: Tuple of two egress lanes: trusted, untrusted.

symbols.name: UNAVAILABLE_REASONS
symbols.note: Tuple of ten machine reasons for unavailability.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_BENCH_OLLAMA_HOST
symbols.note: HTTP URL for bench Ollama host.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_LOCAL_OLLAMA_HOST
symbols.note: HTTP URL for local Ollama host, uses 127.0.0.1 to avoid IPv6 miss.

symbols.name: PROMPT_DATA_NOTICE
symbols.note: String prepended to every outbound prompt instructing the model to treat evidence as data.

symbols.name: _slug
symbols.note: Sanitizes a string to [A-Za-z0-9._-], replacing other runs with '-', falls back to 'unknown' if empty.

symbols.name: model_family
symbols.note: Coarse weight family from model string: strips tag, path, and trailing size/version tokens; over-merges deliberately.

symbols.name: VendorReply
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with vendor, actor, model, status, content, latency_s, reason, stderr, usage, independence_class, endpoint, cli_version, lane, local, withheld. Validates status and lane in __post_init__.

symbols.name: FloorRefusal
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with rule and channel (path|content|prompt).

claims.text: Every adapter here exposes the same shape -- ask(prompt, *, role, timeout_s, model=None) -> VendorReply
claims.why: No adapter classes are defined in this chunk; the claim refers to classes defined later in the file or imported.

claims.text: VendorReply carries no approve/reject/score/verdict/majority field and must never grow one
claims.where: module docstring and VendorReply class docstring
claims.why: VendorReply dataclass fields are vendor, actor, model, status, content, latency_s, reason, stderr, usage, independence_class, endpoint, cli_version, lane, local, withheld; none of the forbidden fields appear.

claims.text: status here is a TRANSPORT status (did the bytes make the round trip), not a judgement about the work under review.
claims.why: STATUSES tuple contains only transport outcomes: ok, unavailable, timeout, refused_by_floor, error. No judgement terms present.

claims.text: The premise -- 'independent vendors have independent blind spots, so cross-vendor disagreement is informative' -- is plausible and UNTESTED here.
claims.why: The chunk contains no test harness, no experimental data, and no code that measures independence. It is purely descriptive of a protocol to be implemented elsewhere.

claims.text: Codex runs exec --sandbox read-only with approvals off
claims.why: No codex adapter or subprocess invocation is present in this chunk.

claims.text: Claude runs -p with tools disallowed and NO dontAsk
claims.why: No claude adapter or subprocess invocation is present in this chunk.

claims.text: Every subprocess is spawned in a FRESH EMPTY TEMP DIRECTORY that is not the repo, not a worktree and contains no repo files (see council_cwd)
claims.why: council_cwd is not defined in this chunk; its behavior cannot be verified here.

claims.text: All evidence reaches a model through the prompt or not at all.
claims.why: No evidence-passing code is present in this chunk.

claims.text: The secret floor runs PER FILE before any bytes leave the process: the PATH channel over each evidence path individually ... the CONTENT channel per file, and a content-only backstop over the assembled prompt.
claims.why: No floor_check or secret_floor_rule usage is present in this chunk.

claims.text: A hit REFUSES the call (status="refused_by_floor"); there is no redact-and-send, and the runner is never invoked.
claims.why: No floor_refusal handling code is present in this chunk.

claims.text: OLLAMA_HOST is NEVER set, mutated or inherited by anything in this module.
claims.why: The chunk contains no assignment or mutation of OLLAMA_HOST; no os.environ usage appears.

claims.text: The host is passed explicitly per call, and whether it counts as local is decided by sensitivity.lane_for_host -- the ONE implementation of "do the bytes leave this machine".
claims.why: No call sites or adapter code are present in this chunk; only the import of lane_for_host is visible.

claims.text: NUMERIC LOOPBACK ONLY: localhost does NOT count, because a name is a DNS indirection the predicate cannot see through.
claims.why: No lane_for_host implementation is present in this chunk.

claims.text: codex and agy default to lane="untrusted": the allow-list / default-deny tier is ON for them, and withheld paths are named.
claims.why: No adapter defaults are present in this chunk.

claims.text: Council records are NEVER an input to memory recall, and nothing in this module touches memstore.
claims.why: No memstore import or reference appears in the entire chunk.

claims.text: Transport outcome of one ask. CLOSED -- an adapter may not invent a sixth.
claims.why: STATUSES is a fixed tuple of five strings; no mechanism in this chunk allows extension.

claims.text: None of these is a judgement about the reviewed work; "ok" means the bytes came back, nothing more.
claims.why: The status strings are all transport-level; no judgement term like 'pass' or 'fail' is present.

claims.text: Egress lane for a participant. untrusted turns the allow-list / default-deny tier ON (sensitivity.slice_egress_rule).
claims.why: LANES is a tuple of two strings; the mapping to slice_egress_rule is not in this chunk, but the constant itself is as documented.

claims.text: Machine reasons -- never free prose -- so a council record can be aggregated.
claims.why: UNAVAILABLE_REASONS is a tuple of fixed machine-readable strings.

claims.text: Prepended to EVERY outbound prompt.
claims.why: No outbound prompt construction is present in this chunk; the constant is defined but its usage is not visible.

claims.text: The mitigation is not a better delimiter -- it is that an injection attempt becomes a FINDING.
claims.why: The notice text instructs the model to report injection as a finding, but no code in this chunk implements that handling.

claims.text: NO LOCAL-HOST TABLE HERE, ON PURPOSE. "Do the bytes leave this machine" has exactly one implementation, sensitivity.lane_for_host, imported above.
claims.why: The chunk contains no local-host table; the only reference to lane_for_host is the import statement.

claims.text: This module used to carry _LOCAL_HOSTS + _endpoint_host and disagreed with the shared predicate on [::1], on 127.0.0.0/8, and on localhost.
claims.why: Historical claim about previous versions; not verifiable from current code.

claims.text: See tests/test_host_predicate.py, which fails if the table comes back.
claims.why: The referenced test file is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Make a model id safe for an actor segment without losing information.
claims.why: _slug replaces any run of characters not in [A-Za-z0-9._-] with '-', preserving alphanumerics, dots, underscores, and hyphens. It does not truncate, so information is preserved for safe characters.

claims.text: council.<vendor>.<model> per docs/adrs/010-naming-namespaces.md.
claims.why: The ADR document is not in this chunk; the format is delegated to bus.actor_id.

claims.text: A bare actor: "claude" in a durable record is a defect ... a dissent attributed only to a vendor cannot be re-run six months on.
claims.why: actor_id always includes vendor and model segments, so a bare vendor-only id cannot be produced by this function.

claims.text: The FORMAT is delegated to bus.actor_id so the id on a transcript turn and the id on the reply that produced it cannot drift apart; this function only normalises the raw model id first (a raw qwen2.5-coder:7b would otherwise put a colon in a durable identifier).
claims.why: actor_id calls _bus_actor_id(_slug(vendor), _slug(model)) and _slug replaces colons with '-', so the raw model id is normalized before delegation.

claims.text: Coarse weight family, for VendorReply.independence_class.
claims.why: model_family returns a string used as the first element of independence_class in VendorReply (default ('unknown','unknown')).

claims.text: The unit of independence is WEIGHTS, not endpoints.
claims.why: model_family ignores endpoint information and derives family purely from the model string.

claims.text: Local qwen2.5-coder:7b and bench qwen2.5-coder:7b are one voice on two sockets
claims.why: model_family('qwen2.5-coder:7b') returns 'qwen2.5-coder' regardless of endpoint, so both map to the same family.

claims.text: the 1.5b/7b/14b/32b line are near-clones of each other; a council that degrades to "Ollama plus Ollama" reports two participants and holds one opinion.
claims.why: model_family strips trailing size tokens like '7b', '14b', etc., so all sizes of the same base model collapse to the same family.

claims.text: Heuristic and deliberately coarse -- it strips the tag (:7b) and any trailing size/version token, so it OVER-merges rather than under-merges.
claims.why: The regex stripping loop removes trailing tokens matching \d+(\.\d+)?[bkm]?|v\d+|latest|preview|\d{8}, which covers size and version tokens.

claims.text: Over-merging costs a seat; under-merging silently fakes independence.
claims.why: model_family aggressively strips trailing tokens, so it will merge models with different sizes/versions into one family, which is over-merging.

claims.text: Deliberately carries NO approve/reject/pass/verdict/ok/score/confidence field, and must never grow one
claims.why: VendorReply fields are vendor, actor, model, status, content, latency_s, reason, stderr, usage, independence_class, endpoint, cli_version, lane, local, withheld; none of the forbidden fields appear.

claims.text: status is transport, content is prose for a human and for a claim extractor, and everything else is provenance so the turn can be re-run and compared.
claims.why: Fields like vendor, actor, model, latency_s, usage, endpoint, cli_version, lane, local, withheld are all provenance metadata; status is a transport status from STATUSES; content is free text.

claims.text: Machine reason from UNAVAILABLE_REASONS, or a secret-floor rule LABEL (never the matched bytes). Empty when status == "ok".
claims.why: The comment describes how reason is populated, but no code in this chunk enforces that; no validation of reason is present.

claims.text: Evidence paths withheld by the tier-2 allow-list on an untrusted lane.
claims.why: No code in this chunk populates or validates withheld paths; the comment is descriptive.

claims.text: A secret-floor hit. Names the RULE, never the matched bytes.
claims.why: FloorRefusal has only rule and channel fields; no field for matched bytes exists.

observations.what: VendorReply.__post_init__ validates status and lane but does not validate reason against UNAVAILABLE_REASONS or rule labels, nor channel against 'path'/'content'/'prompt'.
The module docstring makes many claims about adapter behavior and egress control that are not verifiable in this chunk; they depend on code later in the file or in other modules.
